sources.entry: NotchOTP - Native TOTP authenticator with a notch-sized panel, keyboard shortcuts, and local Keychain storage. ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.one_liner: NotchOTP is a native macOS TOTP authenticator that shows one-time codes in a panel that drops down from the MacBook notch, opened with a global shortcut.
summary.what_it_does: The app opens a black, notch-width panel with Control + Option + Space and shows the current TOTP code with a circular countdown. You can type to search accounts, switch between them with Tab, and press Enter to copy the code and return to the previous app. Accounts are added by manual entry of service, name and Base32 secret, by pasting an otpauth:// link, or by importing a QR image through Apple Vision. Secrets and account metadata are stored in the macOS Keychain. The README says the app makes no network requests and has no analytics. It supports SHA-1, SHA-256 and SHA-512, 6 or 8 digits, and a configurable period, and the interface is available in six languages.
use_cases: Get two-factor login codes without leaving the keyboard
Store TOTP secrets locally in the macOS Keychain
Import a 2FA QR code from an image file
Copy a one-time code quickly into a login form
Replace a phone-based authenticator for Mac workflows
notable: Panel sized to the physical notch, with a top-centred fallback on displays without a notch
Keyboard-first flow: global shortcut, Tab switching, search, Enter to copy
Clipboard contents marked concealed and transient, and cleared when the code expires
Covers all 18 RFC 6238 Appendix B test vectors in its test suite
Demo mode with public fixtures that never touches the real vault
caveats: Apple Silicon release only; the initial version was tested on macOS 26.5
Not implemented: HOTP, Steam Guard, Google Authenticator migration batches, cloud sync and secret export
Described as an early version, not independently audited
Rebuilding an ad-hoc-signed app can make macOS ask again for Keychain access
